import numpy as np


def r(x):
    # Maps x in [0, 1] to 1 - x, which corresponds to t -> -t
    return 1.0 - float(x)


def R(y_orig, y_new):
    # Since tanh(t) is an odd function and the surrogate model is trained on noiseless
    # data, the fitted polynomial is highly symmetric (odd), conserving the property
    # program(x) + program(1-x) ≈ 0.
    return abs(y_orig + y_new) < 0.08
